headline: Consumer Prices Rose 3.7 Percent on the Year as the 10-Year Yield Rose to 5.33 Percent
narrative: September consumer prices rose 0.6 percent and 3.7 percent over the year, up from 3.4 percent. Gasoline rose 9.1 percent and accounted for over half of the monthly increase, so the inflation pipe is fuel inside a higher yearly rate, and the cost of money moved with the print: the 10-year yield rose to 5.33 percent from 5.23 percent and the dollar index rose to 102.79 from 102.21. Bitcoin changed hands near 82k after a session high near 84k.
author: jordan
